title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: How to check if a string contains particular strings (if a string is a substring of another)
summary: This post explains two methods to check if a string contains a substring in Business Central using AL code: the Text.StrPos method returns the position of the first occurrence, while Text.Contains returns a boolean value. Both approaches are demonstrated with table extension examples.
key_points: Text.StrPos(Text, Text) searches for the first occurrence of a substring and returns its position, or zero if not found
Text.Contains(Text) is a simpler alternative that directly returns whether a substring occurs in the string
For case-insensitive searches, use Text.LowerCase or Text.UpperCase to convert strings before comparing
Both methods return zero or false if the string or substring is empty

quotes.text: Text.StrPos(Text, Text) Method: Searches for the first occurrence of substring inside a string.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is one of two main approaches for finding substrings, showing the foundational method available in AL

quotes.text: Text.Contains(Text) Method: Returns a value indicating whether a specified substring occurs within this string.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the simpler, more modern alternative method that directly answers the question of substring existence
